claims.evidence: This claim is supported by measurements shown in Figure 3D-E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D-E.

claims.claim: Reductions in both total cross-sectional brain area and cortical thickness were observed in +/K1918X brains.
claims.source: We observed reductions in both total cross-sectional brain area (Figure 3F–G) and cortical thickness (Figure 3H–I) in +/K1918X brains
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Nissl staining analysis shown in Figure 3F-I.

claims.claim: Significant decreases in cortical layer 2/3 and layer 5 thickness were observed in +/K1918X brains.
claims.source: Significant decreases in cortical layer 2/3 and layer 5 thickness were observed in +/K1918X brains (Figure 3H–J)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Nissl staining analysis shown in Figure 3H-J.

claims.claim: No significant differences in brain area or cortical thickness were observed in either +/K1431M or +/M2145T mice.
claims.source: Meanwhile, no significant differences in brain area or cortical thickness were observed in either +/K1431M or +/M2145T mice.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Nissl staining analysis shown in Figure 3F-I.

claims.claim: No change in total cortical cell density or in layer-specific cell density was observed in heterozygous Trio variant male mice.
claims.source: However, we observed no change in total cortical cell density or in layer-specific cell density in heterozygous Trio variant male mice, nor were numbers of cortical NeuN +neuronal cells or PV +inhibitory neurons altered relative to WT
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H-N.

claims.claim: Sholl analysis of M1 L5 PNs revealed significant reductions in both basal and apical dendritic arbor complexity and dendritic field size in P42 +/K1918X neurons.
claims.source: Sholl analysis of M1 L5 PNs revealed significant reductions in both basal and apical dendritic arbor complexity and dendritic field size in P42 +/K1918X neurons
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by dendritic arbor reconstruction and Sholl analysis data shown in Figure 3K-O.

claims.claim: Sholl analysis revealed an increase in proximal basal arbor complexity in +/K1431M neurons.
claims.source: an increase in proximal basal arbor complexity in +/K1431M neurons
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by dendritic arbor reconstruction and Sholl analysis data shown in Figure 3K-O.

claims.claim: Sholl analysis revealed a decrease in distal apical arbor complexity and apical dendritic field size in +/M2145T neurons relative to WT.
claims.source: and a decrease in distal apical arbor complexity and apical dendritic field size in +/M2145T neurons relative to WT (Figure 3K–O, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by dendritic arbor reconstruction and Sholl analysis data shown in Figure 3K-O and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: None of the Trio variant heterozygotes exhibited altered dendritic spine density on M1 L5 pyramidal neurons compared to WT mice on either apical or basal secondary arbors.
claims.source: Notably, none of the Trio variant heterozygotes exhibited altered dendritic spine density on M1 L5 pyramidal neurons compared to WT mice on either apical or basal secondary arbors (Figure 3—figure supplement 2L and M).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by dendritic spine density analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2L and M.

claims.claim: Synapse density was significantly increased in +/K1918X mice compared to WT.
claims.source: Electron microscopy of cortical area M1 L5 revealed that synapse density was significantly increased in +/K1918X mice compared to WT (Figure 4A and B)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claims.claim: Postsynaptic density (PSD) length was slightly decreased in +/K1918X (by 6%) and +/M2145T (by 6.6%) mice relative to WT.
claims.source: Within synapses, postsynaptic density (PSD) length was slightly decreased in +/K1918X (by 6%) and +/M2145T (by 6.6%) mice relative to WT, but not in +/K1431M mice (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy measurements shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Cross-sectional presynaptic bouton area and spine head area were similar to WT in each Trio variant heterozygote.
claims.source: Cross-sectional presynaptic bouton area and spine head area were similar to WT in each Trio variant heterozygote (Figure 4D and E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy measurements shown in Figure 4D and E.

claims.claim: The densities of both docked and tethered vesicles at 15 and 50 nm from the active zone were significantly increased in +/M2145T relative to the other genotypes.
claims.source: The densities of both docked and tethered vesicles at 15 and 50 nm from the active zone (AZ) respectively, which together can estimate the readily releasable pool (RRP) (Montesinos et al., 2015; Dong et al., 2018), were significantly increased in +/M2145T relative to the other genotypes (Figure 4F and G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy measurements of synaptic vesicle distribution shown in Figure 4F and G.

claims.claim: SV distribution at 200 nm from the AZ was significantly increased in +/M2145T mice, suggesting an overall larger SV pool size.
claims.source: Also, SV distribution at 200 nm from the AZ, thought to contribute the reserve pool, was also significantly increased in +/M2145T mice, suggesting an overall larger SV pool size.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy measurements shown in Figure 4F and is an inference from the data.

claims.claim: AMPAR-mediated mEPSC amplitudes were significantly increased in +/K1431M and +/K1918X mice relative to WT littermates, with no change in their frequencies.
claims.source: AMPAR-mediated mEPSC amplitudes were significantly increased in +/K1431M and +/K1918X mice relative to WT littermates, with no change in their frequencies (Figure 5A–C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5A-C.

claims.claim: AMPAR-mediated mEPSC amplitudes were unchanged in +/M2145T mice, but their frequencies were significantly increased.
claims.source: In contrast, AMPAR-mediated mEPSC amplitudes were unchanged in +/M2145T mice, but their frequencies were significantly increased.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5A-C.

claims.claim: No significant changes in NMDAR mEPSC amplitudes were noted.
claims.source: No significant changes in NMDAR mEPSC amplitudes were noted
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5D-F.

claims.claim: NMDAR mEPSC frequencies were decreased in +/K1431M and increased in +/M2145T mice cortex.
claims.source: while NMDAR mEPSC frequencies were decreased in +/K1431M and increased in +/M2145T mice cortex (Figure 5D–F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5D-F.

claims.claim: +/K1431M and +/K1918X Trio variant heterozygotes showed decreased NMDA/AMPA ratios.
claims.source: +/K1431M and +/K1918X Trio variant heterozygotes showed decreased NMDA/AMPA ratios, indicating imbalances in NMDAR- versus AMPAR-mediated conductance (Figure 5J and K)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5J and K.

claims.claim: Significant decreases in mIPSC frequencies were noted in +/K1431M and +/M2145T mice relative to WT mice, with no change in amplitudes.
claims.source: Significant decreases in mIPSC frequencies were noted in +/K1431M and +/M2145T mice relative to WT mice, with no change in amplitudes (Figure 5G–I).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5G-I.

claims.claim: +/K1918X mice exhibited increased mIPSC amplitude with no observed change in mIPSC frequency.
claims.source: +/K1918X mice exhibited increased mIPSC amplitude with no observed change in mIPSC frequency.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5G-I.

claims.claim: LTP was robustly induced and potentiated in M1 L5 PNs from WT mice.
claims.source: While LTP was robustly induced and potentiated in M1 L5 PNs from WT mice
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5L and M.

claims.claim: LTP induction and potentiation were deficient in slices from +/K1918X and +/K1431M mutant mice.
claims.source: LTP induction and potentiation were deficient in slices from +/K1918X and +/K1431M mutant mice.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5L and M.

claims.claim: +/M2145T L5 PNs showed increased induction and prolonged potentiation of LTP compared to WT L5 PNs.
claims.source: In contrast, +/M2145T L5 PNs showed increased induction and prolonged potentiation of LTP compared to WT L5 PNs.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 5L and M.

claims.claim: Trio localizes presynaptically and interacts with the presynaptic active zone scaffolding proteins Bassoon and Piccolo.
claims.source: In addition to its postsynaptic roles, Trio localizes presynaptically and interacts with the presynaptic active zone scaffolding proteins Bassoon and Piccolo (Terry-Lorenzo et al., 2016; O'Neil et al., 2021; Paskus et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research (Terry-Lorenzo et al., 2016; O'Neil et al., 2021; Paskus et al., 2019).

claims.claim: Rac1 activity levels can bidirectionally affect SV probability of release (Pr) in excitatory synapses.
claims.source: Additionally, recent work demonstrates that Rac1 activity levels can bidirectionally affect SV probability of release (Pr) in excitatory synapses (O'Neil et al., 2021; Keine et al., 2022; Broadbelt et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research (O'Neil et al., 2021; Keine et al., 2022; Broadbelt et al., 2002).

claims.claim: PPF was significantly enhanced in +/K1431M M1 L5 PNs at short ISIs relative to WT, suggesting a reduction in Pr at these synapses.
claims.source: PPF was significantly enhanced in +/K1431M M1 L5 PNs at short ISIs relative to WT, suggesting a reduction in Pr at these synapses (Figure 6A and B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by paired-pulse ratio measurements shown in Figure 6A and B, with inference about Pr.

claims.claim: The +/M2145T PPR curve was complex, with significantly reduced PPF at short ISIs, yet clearly increased PPF at longer ISIs compared to WT.
claims.source: The +/M2145T PPR curve was complex, with significantly reduced PPF at short ISIs, yet clearly increased PPF at longer ISIs compared to WT (Figure 6A and B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by paired-pulse ratio measurements shown in Figure 6A and B.

claims.claim: The decreased PPF at initial ISIs in +/M2145T mice, together with an increase in both AMPAR and NMDAR mEPSC frequency, demonstrates an increase in both synchronous and spontaneous glutamate Pr.
claims.source: The decreased PPF at initial ISIs in +/M2145T mice, together with an increase in both AMPAR and NMDAR mEPSC frequency (Figure 5A–C), demonstrates an increase in both synchronous and spontaneous glutamate Pr.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by paired-pulse ratio and mEPSC data, with inference about Pr.

claims.claim: Glutamate Pr in the L2/3-L5 synapses was increased in +/M2145T mice, while it was decreased for +/K1431M mice.
claims.source: Glutamate Pr in the L2/3-L5 synapses was increased in +/M2145T mice, while it was decreased for +/K1431M mice (Figure 6E)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Pr estimates from high-frequency stimulation trains shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: RRP size was much larger in L2/3-L5 synapses of +/M2145T mice relative to WT.
claims.source: RRP size was much larger in L2/3-L5 synapses of +/M2145T mice relative to WT (Figure 6F)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RRP estimates from high-frequency stimulation trains shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: The recovery rate (τR) was significantly slower in +/K1431M L5 PNs, and they did not recover to their initial strength within 18 s, plateauing at 78% of maximal recovery compared to WT.
claims.source: The recovery rate (τR) was significantly slower in +/K1431M L5 PNs, and they did not recover to their initial strength within 18 s, plateauing at 78% of maximal recovery compared to WT (Figure 6G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by fractional recovery measurements shown in Figure 6G.

claims.claim: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) revealed alterations in distinct functions for each Trio variant.
claims.source: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA; Subramanian et al., 2005; Mootha et al., 2003) revealed alterations in distinct functions for each Trio variant (Figure 7A; Figure 7—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA results shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: The only enriched gene set specific to neurons was downregulation of the synaptic vesicle pathway in +/K1431M cortex.
claims.source: Of note, the only enriched gene set specific to neurons was downregulation of the synaptic vesicle pathway in +/K1431M cortex; all other gene sets were not cell-type specific.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA results shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: All three Trio variant heterozygotes showed enrichment of differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) in synaptic processes when restricted to brain-specific genes.
claims.source: When restricted to brain-specific genes, all three Trio variant heterozygotes showed enrichment of differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) in synaptic processes (Figure 7B and C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by SynGO analysis shown in Figure 7B and C.

claims.claim: +/M2145T upregulated DEPs and +/K1431M downregulated DEPs were significantly enriched at the presynapse.
claims.source: Notably, +/M2145T upregulated DEPs and +/K1431M downregulated DEPs were significantly enriched at the presynapse (Figure 7B)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by SynGO analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: Only +/K1431M downregulated DEPs showed significant enrichment for postsynaptic receptor and synaptic vesicle cycling.
claims.source: but with only +/K1431M downregulated DEPs showing significant enrichment for postsynaptic receptor and synaptic vesicle cycling (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by SynGO analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: +/K1918X showed enrichment of DEPs at the postsynapse, particularly in the postsynaptic density.
claims.source: Meanwhile, +/K1918X showed enrichment of DEPs at the postsynapse, particularly in the postsynaptic density (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by SynGO analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: Munc18-1, Syt3, and Syp levels were increased in +/M2145T synaptosomes relative to WT.
claims.source: Munc18-1, Syt3, and Syp levels were increased in +/M2145T synaptosomes relative to WT (Figure 7D–H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data from synaptosomes shown in Figure 7D-H.

claims.claim: Stx1a levels were significantly decreased in +/K1431M synaptosomes compared to WT.
claims.source: Meanwhile, Stx1a levels were significantly decreased in +/K1431M synaptosomes compared to WT, with no significant changes in +/K1918X compared to WT mice.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data from synaptosomes shown in Figure 7D-H.

claims.claim: Levels of the Rac1 GEF Tiam1 were increased in both +/K1431M and +/M2145T P42 cortical lysates.
claims.source: Indeed, levels of the Rac1 GEF Tiam1 were increased in both +/K1431M and +/M2145T P42 cortical lysates
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7I-L.

claims.claim: VAV2 levels were increased in +/M2145T P42 lysates.
claims.source: while VAV2 levels were increased in +/M2145T P42 lysates (Figure 7I–L).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7I-L.

claims.claim: Levels of the Trio paralog Kalirin were unaffected in the Trio variant mice at P42.
claims.source: Levels of the Trio paralog Kalirin (Yan et al., 2015) were unaffected in the Trio variant mice at P42 (Figure 7J).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7J.

claims.claim: Rac1 negatively regulates synaptic vesicle replenishment and synaptic strength in excitatory synapses.
claims.source: Rac1 negatively regulates synaptic vesicle replenishment and synaptic strength in excitatory synapses (O'Neil et al., 2021; Keine et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research (O'Neil et al., 2021; Keine et al., 2022).

claims.claim: Treatment of +/K1431M and WT slices acutely with NSC shifted the PPF downwards in M1 L5 PNs, suggesting an increase in Pr in both cases.
claims.source: Treatment of +/K1431M and WT slices acutely with NSC shifted the PPF downwards in M1 L5 PNs, suggesting an increase in Pr in both cases (Figure 8A and B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by paired-pulse ratio measurements with NSC treatment shown in Figure 8A and B, with inference about Pr.

claims.claim: Application of NSC to WT and +/K1431M slices under HFS train stimulation decreased initial facilitation in both and significantly increased Pr without affecting RRP size in both, rescuing the initial Pr in +/K1431M slices.
claims.source: Application of NSC to WT and +/K1431M slices under HFS train stimulation decreased initial facilitation in both (Figure 8C and D), and significantly increased Pr (Figure 8E) without affecting RRP size (Figure 8F) in both, rescuing the initial Pr in +/K1431M slices (Figure 8C–F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by high-frequency stimulation data with NSC treatment shown in Figure 8C-F.

claims.claim: NSC treatment increased the fractional recovery rate (τR) in both WT and +/K1431M slices.
claims.source: NSC treatment increased the fractional recovery rate (τR) in both WT and +/K1431M slices (WT +NSC: 32% faster than WT; +/K1431M+NSC: 40% faster than +/K1431M).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by fractional recovery measurements with NSC treatment shown in Figure 8G.

claims.claim: NSC treatment of the +/K1431M variant allowed for full recovery at 18 s interval and sped up the recovery rate, but it remained significantly slower compared to WT (by 45%).
claims.source: NSC treatment of the +/K1431M variant allowed for full recovery at 18 s interval and sped up the recovery rate, but it remained significantly slower compared to WT (by 45%; Figure 8G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by fractional recovery measurements with NSC treatment shown in Figure 8G.

claims.claim: Presynaptic Trio GEF1-dependent Rac1 signaling is crucial for maintaining synchronous glutamate Pr and SV replenishment at cortical L2/3-L5 synapses.
claims.source: Overall, we demonstrate that presynaptic Trio GEF1-dependent Rac1 signaling is crucial for maintaining synchronous glutamate Pr and SV replenishment at cortical L2/3-L5 synapses.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the combined data from paired-pulse ratio, high-frequency stimulation, and NSC rescue experiments.

claims.claim: Large-scale genetic studies show significant overlap in risk genes for ASD, SCZ, and BPD, many converging on synaptic proteins.
claims.source: Large-scale genetic studies show significant overlap in risk genes for ASD, SCZ, and BPD, many converging on synaptic proteins (Carroll and Owen, 2009; Purcell et al., 2014; Satterstrom et al., 2020; Genovese et al., 2016; Fromer et al., 2014; De Rubeis et al., 2014; Iossifov et al., 2014; Pinto et al., 2014; Kirov et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple large-scale genetic studies.

claims.claim: Mice heterozygous for NDD-associated Trio variants differentially affecting Trio protein levels or GEF activity yield overlapping but distinct behavioral, neuroanatomical, and synaptic phenotypes.
claims.source: Our study reveals that mice heterozygous for NDD-associated Trio variants differentially affecting Trio protein levels or GEF activity yield overlapping but distinct behavioral, neuroanatomical, and synaptic phenotypes.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the comprehensive comparison of phenotypes across the three Trio variants throughout the manuscript.

claims.claim: Trio is critical for postsynaptic signaling and synaptic plasticity.
claims.source: Our findings extend prior work demonstrating that Trio is critical for postsynaptic signaling and synaptic plasticity.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research and the current study's findings on mEPSCs and LTP.

claims.claim: Trio is critical for glutamate release and synaptic vesicle recycling.
claims.source: We also demonstrate for the first time in mice that Trio is critical for glutamate release and synaptic vesicle recycling
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by paired-pulse ratio, high-frequency stimulation, and synaptic vesicle distribution data.

claims.claim: NDD-associated variants differentially impact pre- and post-synaptic roles of Trio.
claims.source: and that NDD-associated variants differentially impact these pre- and post-synaptic roles.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the differential effects of the three Trio variants on presynaptic and postsynaptic functions throughout the manuscript.

claims.claim: Individuals with mutations in TRIO present with a range of NDD-associated clinical features, including varying degrees of intellectual disability, altered head size, skeletal and facial features, and behavioral abnormalities.
claims.source: Individuals with mutations in TRIO present with a range of NDD-associated clinical features, including varying degrees of intellectual disability, altered head size, skeletal and facial features, and behavioral abnormalities (Ba et al., 2016; Barbosa et al., 2020; Gazdagh et al., 2023; Pengelly et al., 2016; Bircher et al., 2022; Bonnet et al., 2023; Schultz-Rogers et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple clinical studies.

claims.claim: Patients with missense or truncating variants in TRIO that reduce GEF1 activity have mild developmental delay and microcephaly.
claims.source: Patients with missense or truncating variants in TRIO that reduce GEF1 activity have mild developmental delay and microcephaly (Barbosa et al., 2020; Bonnet et al., 2023; Pengelly et al., 2016; Bircher et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claims.claim: The smaller brain size in +/K1918X male mice was associated with a reduction in neuropil and reduced cortical thickness, similar to mice bearing excitatory neuron-specific ablation of one Trio allele and paralleling the reduced gray matter volume and cortical thickness in SCZ patients.
claims.source: The smaller brain size in +/K1918X male mice was associated with a reduction in neuropil and reduced cortical thickness, similar to mice bearing excitatory neuron-specific ablation of one Trio allele (Katrancha et al., 2019) and paralleling the reduced gray matter volume and cortical thickness in SCZ patients (Howes et al., 2023; Dabiri et al., 2022; Harvey et al., 1993; Suddath et al., 1989; Zipursky et al., 1992).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical measurements in the current study and citations to prior research in mice and humans.

claims.claim: Rac1 mediates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion from pancreatic islet beta-cells.
claims.source: Rac1 mediates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion from pancreatic islet beta-cells (Kowluru, 2011; Kowluru, 2021; Zhou et al., 2015; Veluthakal and Thurmond, 2021; Asahara et al., 2013; Sylow et al., 2016)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Chronic alterations in Rac1 activity may contribute to weight changes in Trio +/K1431M and +/K1918X mice.
claims.source: which may explain how chronic alterations in Rac1 activity contribute to weight changes in Trio +/K1431M and +/K1918X mice.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observed weight changes and the known role of Rac1 in insulin secretion.

claims.claim: Rac1 and RhoA signaling is critical for dendrite development.
claims.source: Rac1 and RhoA signaling is critical for dendrite development (Hall, 1998; Luo, 2000; Nakayama et al., 2000; Newey et al., 2005; Ba et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: The reductions in dendritic arborization and length in +/K1918X neurons are consistent with reports of reduced gray matter volume and dendrite alterations in individuals with SCZ versus controls.
claims.source: The reductions in dendritic arborization and length in +/K1918X neurons are consistent with reports of reduced gray matter volume and dendrite alterations in individuals with SCZ versus controls (Broadbelt et al., 2002; Black et al., 2004)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by dendritic arbor data in the current study and citations to clinical studies.

claims.claim: Reduced Trio function in other cell types, such as in inhibitory neurons or glia, or in neurons from other brain regions that project to cortical M1 L5 PNs, may ameliorate the phenotypes in excitatory neurons of +/K1918X relative to NEX-Trio+/fl mice.
claims.source: Reduced Trio function in other cell types, such as in inhibitory neurons or glia, or in neurons from other brain regions that project to cortical M1 L5 PNs, may ameliorate the phenotypes in excitatory neurons of +/K1918X relative to NEX-Trio+/fl mice.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of phenotypes between +/K1918X and NEX-Trio+/fl mice.

claims.claim: The K1431M variant significantly reduces TRIO GEF1 nucleotide exchange on Rac1 in vitro.
claims.source: We show here that the K1431M variant significantly reduces TRIO GEF1 nucleotide exchange on Rac1 in vitro, consistent with previous reports (Katrancha et al., 2017; Sadybekov et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro GEF assay data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B and citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Decreased Rac1 activity was observed in +/K1431M mice at embryonic day 14.5 in the ganglionic eminence.
claims.source: Decreased Rac1 activity was observed in +/K1431M mice at embryonic day 14.5 in the ganglionic eminence, which is enriched for pre-migratory GABAergic interneurons (Sun et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research (Sun et al., 2021).

claims.claim: An increase in active Rac1 levels in +/K1431M postnatal brains aligns with observed phenotypes (e.g. reduced Pr) and reveals why reductions in brain volume, dendrites and spines, or AMPAR signaling anticipated from reduced Rac1 activity were not observed in +/K1431M mice.
claims.source: This increase aligns with observed phenotypes (e.g. reduced Pr) and reveals why reductions in brain volume, dendrites and spines, or AMPAR signaling anticipated from reduced Rac1 activity (Chen et al., 2009; Reijnders et al., 2017; Tahirovic et al., 2010; Pennucci et al., 2019; Wiens et al., 2005) were not observed in +/K1431M mice.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the observed increase in Rac1 activity and the absence of expected phenotypes, with citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Homeostatic compensation in Rac1 regulation occurs between birth to adult ages in +/K1431M mice.
claims.source: We propose that the increased Rac1 activity we observed reflects homeostatic compensation in Rac1 regulation occurring between birth to adult ages
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observed increase in Rac1 activity and changes in Rac1 GEF levels.

claims.claim: Changes in Rac1-specific GEFs, for example Tiam1 and Vav2, may contribute to homeostatic compensation in +/K1431M mice.
claims.source: and identify changes in Rac1-specific GEFs, for example Tiam1 and Vav2, that may contribute to this compensation.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observed increases in Tiam1 and Vav2 levels.

claims.claim: Kalirin does not compensate for the loss of Trio GEF1 activity in adult Trio mutant mice.
claims.source: Importantly, we did not find changes in Kalirin levels in the adult brain of these Trio mutant mice, suggesting that Kalirin does not compensate for the loss of Trio GEF1 activity at this age.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the absence of changes in Kalirin levels.

claims.claim: The synaptic compartment is a key locus of Trio function.
claims.source: We observed a significant reduction in active RhoA only in purified synaptosomes of +/M2145T brains, reflecting the synaptic compartment as a key locus of Trio function.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that RhoA activity changes were only detected in synaptosomes.

claims.claim: The spatiotemporally precise balance of Rac/Rho activity rather than absolute activity levels can mediate cytoskeletal rearrangements.
claims.source: These findings are consistent with recent evidence that the spatiotemporally precise balance of Rac/Rho activity rather than absolute activity levels can mediate cytoskeletal rearrangements (Grubisha et al., 2022; Duman et al., 2015; Ba and Nadif Kasri, 2017; Pertz, 2010).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Alterations in the activity of additional potential TRIO substrates, such as RhoG, Cdc42, and Rac3, could contribute to phenotypes in Trio variant mice.
claims.source: Alterations in the activity of additional potential TRIO substrates, such as RhoG (Bellanger et al., 2000), Cdc42 (Blangy et al., 2000), and the neurodevelopmentally critical Rac3 (Scala et al., 2021; Hajdo-Milasinović et al., 2007; Corbetta et al., 2009), could also contribute to phenotypes in these mice.
claims.evidence: This claim is speculative, suggesting potential mechanisms that could contribute to observed phenotypes.

claims.claim: Altered activation of Rho GTPases is an important mechanism affecting synaptic function in ASD.
claims.source: Our results strongly complement a growing body of evidence showing that altered activation of Rho GTPases is an important mechanism affecting synaptic function in ASD (Bölte et al., 2023; Pinto et al., 2010; Zeidán-Chuliá et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2020; Carbonell et al., 2023; Zamboni et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the current study's findings and citations to prior research.

claims.claim: Rho GTPase signaling is a convergent pathway in ASD and an attractive target for pharmacotherapy for these disorders.
claims.source: This highlights Rho GTPase signaling as a convergent pathway in ASD and therefore an attractive target for pharmacotherapy for these disorders.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the current study's findings and prior research on Rho GTPases in ASD.

claims.claim: Overexpression of a TRIO K1431M variant with reduced GEF1 activity decreased AMPAR-mediated mESPC amplitudes in rat organotypic slices.
claims.source: Overexpression of a TRIO K1431M variant with reduced GEF1 activity decreased AMPAR-mediated mESPC amplitudes in rat organotypic slices (Tian et al., 2021)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research (Tian et al., 2021).

claims.claim: Rac1 activation increased AMPAR amplitudes by promoting synaptic AMPAR clustering.
claims.source: while Rac1 activation increased AMPAR amplitudes by promoting synaptic AMPAR clustering (Wiens et al., 2005; Hussain et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research (Wiens et al., 2005; Hussain et al., 2015).

claims.claim: Synaptic dysfunction in several NDD models is linked to Rho GTPase signaling dysregulation, identifying it as a commonly affected pathway and a potential therapeutic target.
claims.source: Our findings support growing evidence linking synaptic dysfunction in several NDD models to Rho GTPase signaling dysregulation, identifying it as a commonly affected pathway and a potential therapeutic target.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the current study's findings and prior research on Rho GTPases in NDDs.

results.result: Prior research establishes TRIO as a neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) risk gene with two GEF domains (GEF1 activating Rac1/RhoG, GEF2 activating RhoA) that regulate neuronal development and synaptic function. Different TRIO variant types are associated with distinct NDDs, but the impact of heterozygous variants in vivo has not been explored.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C25 are well-supported by extensive citations to prior literature establishing TRIO's role in NDDs, its biochemical functions, and clinical associations. The gap in knowledge (C25) provides clear rationale for the current study. These background claims appropriately contextualize the research.

results.result: Three NDD-associated Trio variants were generated in mice: K1431M (ASD-associated, impairs GEF1 activity), K1918X (SCZ-associated, leads to nonsense-mediated decay), and M2145T (BPD-associated, reduces GEF2 activity). Heterozygous mice for all three variants survived to adulthood. K1918X reduced Trio9 protein levels by ~50%, while K1431M and M2145T did not alter Trio isoform levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C41 are well-supported by in vitro GEF assays (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B), Western blots (Figure 1C-D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D-L), genotyping data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), and citations to prior work. The characterization of the mouse models is thorough and demonstrates successful generation of the intended variants with expected molecular consequences.

results.result: Trio variants differentially impact Rho GTPase activity in the brain. K1918X mice showed decreased Rac1 activity at P0 but not P42. Unexpectedly, K1431M mice exhibited increased Rac1 activity at both P0 (111%) and P42 (150%) despite the variant impairing GEF1 activity in vitro. M2145T mice showed decreased RhoA activity in P42 cortical synaptosomes (73% of WT) but not in whole brain lysates.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C48 are supported by G-LISA assay data (Figure 1E-J). The unexpected increase in Rac1 activity in K1431M mice (C45, C47) is particularly notable and well-documented, representing a key finding that contradicts in vitro predictions. The compartment-specific effects in M2145T mice (C48) are appropriately identified. Statistical significance is reported with appropriate p-values.

results.result: Trio variant mice exhibit distinct behavioral phenotypes modeling NDD symptoms. K1431M and K1918X mice showed impaired motor coordination and learning on the rotarod. K1431M mice of both sexes and K1918X females showed social interaction deficits. K1918X mice of both sexes and M2145T females showed impaired novel object recognition. K1431M and K1918X males exhibited increased compulsive nestlet shredding.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C54 are supported by comprehensive behavioral testing data (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1). The behavioral battery is appropriate for assessing NDD-relevant phenotypes. Statistical analyses using two-way ANOVA with post-hoc tests are appropriate. The sex-specific differences are noted and appropriately reported. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=9-40 per group).

results.result: Trio variants differentially affect brain and head size. K1431M mice showed reduced head width and brain weight relative to body weight, driven by increased body weight. K1918X mice showed reduced brain weight-to-body weight ratio, reduced cortical thickness, and decreased layer 2/3 and layer 5 thickness. M2145T mice showed no significant changes. No changes in cortical cell density or neuron numbers were observed in any variant.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C61 are supported by anatomical measurements (Figure 3A-J, Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and immunostaining analysis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H-N). The normalization to body weight is appropriate given the weight differences. The finding that K1918X brain size reduction is due to neuropil loss rather than cell number changes (C61) is well-supported. Statistical analyses are appropriate.

results.result: Trio variants cause modest but distinct changes in dendritic arbor morphology of M1 L5 pyramidal neurons. K1918X neurons showed reduced basal and apical dendritic arbor complexity and field size. K1431M neurons showed increased proximal basal arbor complexity. M2145T neurons showed decreased distal apical arbor complexity and field size. No changes in dendritic spine density were observed in any variant.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C65 are supported by dendritic arbor reconstructions and Sholl analysis (Figure 3K-O, Figure 3—figure supplement 1-2). The use of Thy1-GFP mice for visualization is appropriate. The finding of no changes in spine density (C65) is notable given prior work with conditional knockouts. Statistical analyses using one-way and two-way ANOVA are appropriate. Sample sizes (n=15-22 neurons per group) are adequate.

results.result: Electron microscopy revealed ultrastructural synaptic changes in Trio variant mice. K1918X mice showed increased synapse density and slightly decreased PSD length. M2145T mice showed increased densities of docked and tethered vesicles at the active zone (readily releasable pool) and increased reserve pool vesicles. Presynaptic bouton and spine head areas were unchanged in all variants.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C70 are supported by electron microscopy data (Figure 4). The measurements are appropriate and well-quantified. The interpretation that increased docked/tethered vesicles represent an enlarged RRP (C69) is consistent with established methods. The inference about larger SV pool size in M2145T (C70) is reasonable given the data. Sample sizes (5-18 fields per mouse, n=15-30 synapses) are adequate for EM analysis.

results.result: Trio variants differentially affect excitatory and inhibitory synaptic transmission. K1431M and K1918X mice showed increased AMPAR mEPSC amplitudes with no frequency changes, while M2145T showed increased AMPAR mEPSC frequency with unchanged amplitudes. NMDAR mEPSC frequencies were decreased in K1431M and increased in M2145T. K1431M and K1918X showed decreased NMDA/AMPA ratios. mIPSC frequencies were decreased in K1431M and M2145T, while K1918X showed increased mIPSC amplitude.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C77 are supported by comprehensive electrophysiological recordings (Figure 5A-I). The recordings are technically sound with appropriate controls (TTX, receptor antagonists). Statistical analyses are appropriate. Sample sizes (n=9-26 neurons from ≥5-8 mice per group) are adequate. The differential effects on AMPAR vs NMDAR and excitatory vs inhibitory transmission are well-documented and represent important findings.

results.result: Trio variants differentially affect long-term potentiation (LTP) in M1 L5 pyramidal neurons. WT mice showed robust LTP induction and potentiation. K1431M and K1918X mice showed deficient LTP induction and potentiation. M2145T mice showed increased LTP induction and prolonged potentiation compared to WT.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C80 are supported by LTP recordings following theta-burst stimulation (Figure 5L-M). The protocol is appropriate and the results are clear. Statistical analysis using repeated measures two-way ANOVA is appropriate. Sample sizes (n=6-8 neurons from ≥4-5 mice per group) are adequate for LTP experiments. The bidirectional effects on LTP are striking and well-documented.

results.result: Trio variants differentially affect presynaptic glutamate release. K1431M mice showed enhanced paired-pulse facilitation at short ISIs, suggesting reduced probability of release (Pr). M2145T mice showed a complex PPR curve with reduced PPF at short ISIs and increased PPF at longer ISIs, indicating increased Pr and larger readily releasable pool (RRP). High-frequency stimulation confirmed decreased Pr in K1431M and increased Pr and RRP in M2145T. K1431M mice showed slower recovery rate after depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C88 are supported by paired-pulse ratio measurements (Figure 6A-B) and high-frequency stimulation analysis (Figure 6C-G). The use of the 'Decay' method to estimate Pr and RRP is appropriate and well-cited. The inferences about Pr from PPR data (C83, C85) are standard interpretations. Statistical analyses are appropriate. Sample sizes (n=12-34 neurons from ≥5-9 mice per group) are adequate. These findings represent novel insights into Trio's presynaptic role.

results.result: Proteomic analysis of P21 cortex revealed distinct molecular signatures for each Trio variant. GSEA showed variant-specific pathway alterations, with synaptic vesicle pathway downregulation specific to K1431M. SynGO analysis restricted to brain-specific genes showed enrichment of differentially expressed proteins in synaptic processes for all variants. M2145T upregulated and K1431M downregulated proteins were enriched at the presynapse, while K1918X showed postsynaptic enrichment.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C94 are supported by quantitative proteomics data (Figure 7A-C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1). The proteomics approach is appropriate with adequate sample size (n=4 per genotype). GSEA and SynGO analyses are appropriate bioinformatics tools. The finding of presynaptic enrichment in K1431M and M2145T (C92) aligns well with the electrophysiology data. FDR correction is appropriately applied. The proteomics provides important molecular context for the functional findings.

results.result: Western blot analysis of P42 cortical synaptosomes and lysates revealed variant-specific changes in presynaptic proteins and Rho GEFs. M2145T synaptosomes showed increased Munc18-1, Syt3, and Syp levels. K1431M synaptosomes showed decreased Stx1a levels. Tiam1 levels were increased in both K1431M and M2145T cortical lysates. VAV2 levels were increased in M2145T lysates. Kalirin levels were unchanged in all variants.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C99 are supported by Western blot data from synaptosomes (Figure 7D-H) and cortical lysates (Figure 7I-L). The protein targets are well-chosen and relevant to the observed functional phenotypes. The finding of increased Tiam1 in K1431M (C97) provides a potential mechanism for the unexpected increase in Rac1 activity. Statistical analyses using unpaired t-tests or one-way ANOVA are appropriate. Sample sizes (n=6-14 mice per group) are adequate.

results.result: Acute Rac1 inhibition with NSC23766 rescued glutamate release deficits in K1431M mice. NSC treatment shifted PPF downward in both WT and K1431M slices, suggesting increased Pr. NSC significantly increased Pr without affecting RRP size in both genotypes, rescuing the initial Pr deficit in K1431M. NSC increased the fractional recovery rate in both genotypes but did not fully rescue the slower recovery in K1431M. These results demonstrate that presynaptic Trio GEF1-dependent Rac1 signaling is crucial for maintaining synchronous glutamate Pr and SV replenishment.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C105 are supported by comprehensive rescue experiments using NSC23766 (Figure 8). The pharmacological approach is appropriate and the Rac1 inhibitor is well-characterized. The partial rescue of recovery rate (C104) is notable and suggests additional mechanisms beyond Rac1. Statistical analyses are appropriate. Sample sizes (n=12-18 neurons from ≥5 mice per group) are adequate. This represents a key mechanistic finding linking elevated Rac1 activity to the presynaptic deficits in K1431M mice.

results.result: Heterozygosity for different NDD-associated Trio variants yields overlapping but distinct phenotypes in mice across behavioral, neuroanatomical, and synaptic domains. The variants differentially impact pre- and post-synaptic functions, with K1431M and M2145T showing prominent presynaptic deficits and K1918X showing more postsynaptic effects. These findings demonstrate that discrete TRIO variants cause both shared and distinct defects that may reflect variant-specific NDD clinical phenotypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C6, C10, C107, C110, C150, C152 represent the overarching conclusions of the study. These are well-supported by the comprehensive characterization across multiple experimental modalities (behavior, anatomy, electrophysiology, proteomics). The integration of findings across levels of analysis is appropriate. The conclusion that variants cause overlapping but distinct phenotypes is strongly supported by the data. The link to variant-specific NDD phenotypes is reasonable but somewhat speculative given the mouse model limitations.

results.result: The K1431M variant impairs TRIO GEF1 activity in vitro but paradoxically leads to increased Rac1 activity in postnatal K1431M mouse brains. This increase aligns with observed phenotypes and reveals why anticipated reductions in brain volume, dendrites, and AMPAR signaling were not observed. The increased Rac1 activity reflects homeostatic compensation occurring between birth and adult ages, potentially driven by upregulation of other Rac1 GEFs like Tiam1, while Kalirin does not compensate. Elevated Rac1 activity drives the reduction in synchronous glutamate Pr and SV replenishment in K1431M mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C7-C8, C119-C124, C141 describe a key mechanistic finding of the study. The paradoxical increase in Rac1 activity despite impaired GEF1 function is well-documented by in vitro assays (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B), G-LISA measurements (Figure 1E, G, I), and Western blots showing increased Tiam1 (Figure 7I-L). The homeostatic compensation hypothesis (C122) is reasonable given the developmental time course. The link to presynaptic deficits (C141) is supported by NSC rescue experiments (Figure 8). This represents an important and unexpected finding.

results.result: Trio plays an essential role in presynaptic glutamate release and synaptic vesicle recycling. Trio localizes presynaptically and interacts with active zone proteins. Rac1 activity levels bidirectionally affect SV probability of release in excitatory synapses, negatively regulating synchronous glutamate Pr and SV replenishment. Trio GEF1 and GEF2-mediated Rho GTPase signaling pathways play critical and distinct roles in regulating Pr, RRP size, and SV recycling.
results.evaluation: Claims C11, C81-C82, C100, C105, C109, C140, C149 describe the novel presynaptic role of Trio demonstrated in this study. These claims are supported by paired-pulse ratio data (Figure 6A-B), high-frequency stimulation analysis (Figure 6C-G), synaptic vesicle distribution measurements (Figure 4F-G), and NSC rescue experiments (Figure 8). The prior literature on Trio's presynaptic localization (C81) and Rac1's role in release (C82, C100, C140) is appropriately cited. This represents a major advance in understanding Trio function.

results.result: The phenotypes observed in Trio variant mice parallel clinical features in humans with TRIO mutations. K1431M and K1918X mice show reduced brain size consistent with microcephaly in patients with GEF1-deficient variants. K1918X mice show reduced cortical thickness similar to SCZ patients and NEX-Trio+/fl mice. Weight changes in K1431M and K1918X mice may relate to Rac1's role in insulin secretion. Dendritic alterations in K1918X mice are consistent with reports in SCZ patients.
results.evaluation: Claims C111-C118 appropriately contextualize the mouse findings relative to human clinical phenotypes. The parallels drawn are reasonable and well-supported by citations to clinical literature (C111-C113, C117) and prior mouse studies (C113). The speculation about weight changes relating to Rac1's role in insulin secretion (C114-C115) is reasonable but remains speculative. The comparison to NEX-Trio+/fl mice (C118) is appropriate and highlights the value of studying heterozygous variants.

results.result: The synaptic compartment is a key locus of Trio function, with spatiotemporally precise balance of Rac/Rho activity mediating cytoskeletal rearrangements. Altered Rho GTPase activation is an important mechanism affecting synaptic function in ASD and represents a convergent pathway and potential therapeutic target for NDDs. The findings support growing evidence linking synaptic dysfunction in NDD models to Rho GTPase signaling dysregulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C125-C129, C153 place the findings in broader context regarding Rho GTPase signaling in NDDs. The inference about the synaptic compartment being a key locus (C125) is supported by the synaptosome data. The claims about spatiotemporal balance (C126) and Rho GTPases as a convergent pathway (C128-C129, C153) are well-supported by citations to prior literature and the current findings. The suggestion of Rho GTPases as therapeutic targets (C129, C153) is reasonable but speculative.

results.result: The observed changes in AMPAR-mediated transmission and LTP in Trio variant mice can be explained by altered Rac1 activity and its effects on AMPAR trafficking and synaptic strength. Increased AMPAR in K1431M mice may reflect reduced silent synapses due to increased AMPAR incorporation driven by elevated Rac1. Developmental changes in Rac1 activity in K1918X mice may enhance AMPAR tone and affect LTP. The variants dysregulate excitatory and inhibitory transmission in different patterns, resulting in E/I imbalance.
results.evaluation: Claims C130-C138 provide mechanistic interpretations of the synaptic transmission and plasticity data. The interpretations are reasonable and well-supported by citations to prior work on Rac1's role in AMPAR trafficking (C130-C131, C136) and LTP (C135-C137). The inference about reduced silent synapses in K1431M (C132) is reasonable given the data. The developmental hypothesis for K1918X (C133) is plausible given the time course of Rac1 activity changes. The conclusion about E/I imbalance (C134) is well-supported by the mEPSC and mIPSC data.

results.result: The presynaptic effects of Trio variants can be explained by known roles of Trio, Rac1, and RhoA in regulating exocytosis and neurotransmitter release. Rac1 negatively regulates neurotransmitter release by increasing actin filament assembly at the active zone. In K1431M mice, opposing pre- and post-synaptic effects may mask expected changes in AMPAR mEPSC frequency. In M2145T mice, increased levels of Munc18, Syp, and Syt3 contribute to enhanced Pr and altered SV cycling, with altered Syt3 potentially explaining the unusual PPR.
results.evaluation: Claims C139, C143-C148 provide mechanistic interpretations of the presynaptic findings. The interpretations are reasonable and well-supported by citations to prior work on Trio/Rac1/RhoA in exocytosis (C139-C140, C143-C144). The hypothesis about opposing effects masking frequency changes in K1431M (C145) is plausible. The link between increased presynaptic proteins and enhanced Pr in M2145T (C147) is reasonable. The speculation about Syt3 explaining the unusual PPR (C148) is plausible but remains speculative. The acknowledgment that RhoA's specific role is unclear (C146) is appropriate.

results.result: Large-scale genetic studies show significant overlap in NDD risk genes converging on synaptic proteins. The current findings extend prior work on Trio's postsynaptic roles and demonstrate for the first time that the K1431M lesion in TRIO GEF1 leads to presynaptic deficits due to Rac1 dysregulation, which can be rescued by pharmacological normalization.
results.evaluation: Claims C106, C108, C151 summarize key contextual and concluding points. The claim about overlap in NDD risk genes (C106) is well-supported by citations to large-scale genetic studies. The claim about extending prior work on postsynaptic roles (C108) is appropriate. The claim about demonstrating presynaptic deficits and pharmacological rescue (C151) is well-supported by the NSC experiments (Figure 8) and represents a major finding of the study.

results.result: The manuscript establishes background context about TRIO variants being associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) including schizophrenia, autism spectrum disorder, and intellectual disability, with different variant types linked to specific disorders and clinical features. The study addresses a gap by examining heterozygous TRIO variants in vivo.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge this background, with one stating 'The establishment of TRIO dysfunction in the development of ASD, Schizophrenia, and Bi-polar disorder is very recent and of great interest' and another noting 'Disorder-specific variants have been identified in the TRIO gene.' No concerns were raised about these foundational claims.

results.result: Heterozygosity for different Trio variants impacts motor, social, and cognitive behaviors in distinct ways. +/K1431M and +/K1918X mice showed motor deficits on rotarod, +/K1431M mice of both sexes and +/K1918X females showed social preference deficits, +/K1918X mice and +/M2145T females showed novel object recognition deficits, and +/K1918X and +/K1431M males showed increased compulsive nestlet shredding.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirmed these findings, stating the study 'explores how heterozygosity for specific neurodevelopmental disorder-associated Trio variants affects mouse behavior' and 'reveals distinct impacts on motor, social, and cognitive behaviors linked to clinical phenotypes.' One reviewer noted the authors 'achieved their goal of identifying behavioral...alterations that are disorder/variant specific.'

results.result: Trio variants differentially impact head and brain size, with +/K1431M showing reduced head width and brain weight (driven by increased body weight), +/K1918X showing reduced brain area and cortical thickness with decreased dendritic arbor complexity, and +/M2145T showing decreased apical dendritic arbor complexity. No changes in dendritic spine density were observed in any variant.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledged these neuroanatomical findings as part of the comprehensive analysis, with one stating the study 'explores how heterozygosity...affects...brain structure' and another noting 'various approaches to evaluate the resulting...neuronal morphology...phenotypes.' The findings parallel clinical observations in schizophrenia patients, which reviewers did not question.

results.result: Significant changes in postsynaptic function and plasticity were observed across Trio variants. +/K1431M and +/K1918X showed increased AMPAR mEPSC amplitudes and decreased NMDA/AMPA ratios, while +/M2145T showed increased AMPAR and NMDAR mEPSC frequencies. LTP was deficient in +/K1431M and +/K1918X but enhanced in +/M2145T. All variants showed altered inhibitory transmission patterns.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly recognized these findings, stating 'Findings demonstrate that Trio variants yield unique changes in synaptic plasticity' and noting the study provides 'compelling evidence demonstrating unique alterations of each variant in synaptic functions.' One reviewer emphasized the authors 'achieved their goal of identifying...physiological...alterations that are disorder/variant specific.'

results.result: Distinct changes in presynaptic glutamate release occur in +/K1431M and +/M2145T synapses. +/K1431M showed reduced probability of release (Pr) and slower synaptic vesicle recovery, while +/M2145T showed increased Pr, larger readily releasable pool (RRP), and increased synaptic vesicle densities. This demonstrates Trio's essential role in presynaptic glutamate release.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly highlighted this as a key finding, stating 'Findings demonstrate that Trio variants yield unique changes in...glutamate release, highlighting Trio's critical role in presynaptic function.' One reviewer noted this work 'begins to identify the unique and subtle ways brain function is altered' in different disorders, affirming the presynaptic findings as novel and significant.

results.result: The K1431M variant impairs TRIO GEF1 activity in vitro, but paradoxically, +/K1431M mice exhibit increased Rac1 activity in postnatal brains (111% at P0, 150% at P42) and synaptosomes. In contrast, +/K1918X mice show reduced Trio9 protein levels (~50%) and decreased Rac1 activity at P0 that normalizes by P42. +/M2145T mice show decreased RhoA activity in synaptosomes.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledged these biochemical findings without raising concerns. The paradoxical increase in Rac1 activity in +/K1431M mice despite impaired GEF1 activity is presented as a key mechanistic finding that explains the observed phenotypes, and reviewers accepted this interpretation as part of the comprehensive analysis.

results.result: Acute Rac1 inhibition with NSC23766 rescued glutamate release deficits in +/K1431M cortex, demonstrating that elevated Rac1 activity drives the reduction in synchronous glutamate Pr and synaptic vesicle replenishment. This establishes that presynaptic Trio GEF1-dependent Rac1 signaling is crucial for maintaining glutamate release.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly recognized this as a significant finding, with one stating 'We demonstrate that the +/K1431M lesion in TRIO GEF1 leads to presynaptic deficits due to Rac1 dysregulation, which can be rescued by pharmacological normalization.' This rescue experiment was not questioned and was viewed as supporting the mechanistic conclusions.

results.result: Proteomic analysis revealed distinct molecular changes for each Trio variant. +/K1431M showed downregulation of synaptic vesicle pathway genes and decreased Stx1a levels, while showing increased Tiam1 levels suggesting homeostatic compensation. +/M2145T showed increased levels of presynaptic proteins (Munc18-1, Syt3, Syp) and Tiam1/VAV2. Kalirin levels were unchanged across variants.
results.evaluation: While reviewers acknowledged the proteomic findings as part of the comprehensive analysis, one reviewer noted 'Identification of upregulated (potentially compensating) genes in response to these disorder specific Trio variants is extremely interesting. However, a functional demonstration of compensation is not provided.' This indicates the compensation hypothesis (C122, C123) is interesting but not fully validated, though the descriptive proteomic data itself was accepted.

results.result: The study demonstrates that discrete NDD-associated Trio variants yield overlapping but distinct phenotypes in mice across behavioral, neuroanatomical, and synaptic domains. Trio variants disrupt brain function by impairing Rho GTPase signaling, causing diverse synaptic dysfunction through combined effects on pre- and/or post-synaptic functions, identifying Rho GTPase signaling as a convergent pathway and potential therapeutic target.
results.evaluation: Reviewers strongly endorsed these overarching conclusions, stating 'the results provide compelling evidence demonstrating unique alterations of each variant in synaptic functions and behavior' and 'The authors achieved their goal of identifying behavioral, physiological, and molecular alterations that are disorder/variant specific.' One reviewer emphasized 'The impact of this work is extremely high given the growing appreciation of TRIO dysfunction in a large number of brain-related disorders.'

results.result: Mice heterozygous for all three Trio alleles survived to adulthood. Homozygous K1431M and M2145T mice also survived, though fewer M2145T homozygotes were obtained than expected. K1918X homozygotes were not observed. Alternative splicing generates multiple brain-specific Trio isoforms with varying expression by region and age.
results.evaluation: Reviewers did not raise concerns about these basic characterization findings. The viability data and isoform information provide essential context for the study and were implicitly accepted as part of the model validation.

results.result: The manuscript discusses potential mechanisms and broader implications, including Rac1's role in insulin secretion potentially explaining weight changes, the synaptic compartment as a key locus of Trio function, the importance of spatiotemporal balance of Rac/Rho activity, and Rho GTPase signaling as a convergent pathway in ASD and attractive therapeutic target.
results.evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these interpretive and mechanistic discussions. One reviewer noted 'This work is very interesting in that it begins to identify the unique and subtle ways brain function is altered in ASD, Schizophrenia, and Bi-polar disorder,' implicitly supporting the broader mechanistic framework and therapeutic implications discussed.
